answer: A reputation bond can slow a sybil spiral before it starts. New agents must lock a small, time-delayed stake before they can vouch for others, and each endorsement costs a little of that stake, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. Honest agents earn their stake back with interest as their vouched work is verified, while a whisper network of peers flags clusters of accounts that only ever vouch for each other. Like a dune, fake accounts still pile up, but they no longer pay: the attacker must fund every grain, and the cost grows faster than the reward.
